subject: Traffic tiering & burst-budget intake for ded. sizing — VellumAI
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Ashley Park <ashley@vellumai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Traffic tiering & burst-budget intake for dedicated sizing — VellumAI

Hi Ashley,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To scope Dedicated capacity and give you a defensible burst budget/cost estimate, can you fill in the quick intake below or attach a short sample (JSON/CSV) of recent traffic?

Top-level asks (short answers fine):
- Traffic shape: steady qps vs spiky bursts? Typical baseline qps and peak burst qps (any p95/p99 numbers you have).
- Prompt/response length: median prompt tokens, median response tokens, and any long-tail (>95th pct) examples.
- Session model: are you sessionized (KV cache per session) or stateless? Typical session duration and average requests/session.
- Dayparting/geo: do you have heavy regional skew or predictable time-of-day windows?
- SLA targets: p95 latency target for interactive calls and acceptable cold-start window.
- Fallbacks: degree to which you accept lower-capacity fallback models with degraded quality during peak events.

Attached is a blank intake CSV to paste any token histograms or recent telemetry (vellumai_traffic_sample.csv). If you prefer, send a short recording of the request profile or raw sample.

Goal: I’ll turn this into a concise Dedicated sizing sketch (GPU SKUs, oversubscription assumptions, expected occupied capacity, and a burst cushion) and a one-page ops runbook for the pilot.

Can you return the sample by EOD Monday (Aug 31)? We have a slot on Thurs for a 45-min sizing workshop that would let us finalize a pilot commitment.

Thanks,
Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Pre-Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Attach: vellumai_traffic_sample.csv (CSV skeleton)

From: Ashley Park <ashley@vellumai.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Traffic tiering & burst-budget intake for dedicated sizing — VellumAI

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks — attaching a small sample and a token histogram from last month (token_histogram_q2.csv). High-level answers inline:
- Traffic shape: baseline ~45 qps across our inference endpoint; we see short bursts up to ~2,800 qps (10-15 seconds) around feature launches. P95 burst is ~1,200 qps; p99 is ~2,200 qps.
- Prompt/response lengths: median prompt = 48 tokens, median response = 182 tokens. 95th pct response ~820 tokens (long-form summarization jobs).
- Session model: we use per-user sessions with KV cache for chat (session TTL ~30 minutes); about 60% of calls are session-affine. Average session length around 5 requests.
- Dayparting/geo: traffic concentrated on US east coast; spikes mostly during 10:00–14:00 ET.
- SLA targets: p95 latency target 250ms for conversational flows; can accept 1–2s for long-form summarization.
- Fallbacks: we are open to a lower-cost, reduced-context model for non-core flows but want quality-preserving models for 80% of traffic.

We have a procurement/compliance deadline the week after next, so we need the sketch sooner rather than later. Also looping in procurement (procurement@vellumai.com) for cost lead times.

Thanks,
Ashley

--
Ashley Park
Head of Infrastructure, VellumAI
ashley@vellumai.com
Attach: token_histogram_q2.csv

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Ashley Park <ashley@vellumai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Traffic tiering & burst-budget intake for dedicated sizing — VellumAI

Ashley — really helpful, thanks. A few clarifying items so our sizing sketch hits your procurement timeline:

1) Burst window profile: you mentioned 10–15s bursts to 2.8k qps. Can you confirm whether those bursts are single-region (us-east) or fan-out across multiple AZs? If single-region, we can optimize packing and reduce fallback probability.

2) Long-form jobs (95th=820 tokens): are those often asynchronous (batch) or synchronous interactive flows? If asynchronous, we can propose separate runway for batch workers with higher throughput optimizations.

3) KV cache hit-rate: Could you share an approximate cache hit-rate for session-affine requests (even a percent band is fine)? KV cache hit-rate materially affects per-token compute and effective occupancy.

4) Quality-fallback tolerance: to confirm, you want ~80% of interactive traffic served at top-tier model quality, and the remaining 20% can be routed to smaller quantized variants during exceptional peaks? That will inform our canary/fallback routing policy and burst cushion.

Next steps: I’ll draft a one-page Dedicated footprint sketch by Tue morning (Aug 1 — sorry, typo: Sep 1; intended Sep 1) that includes: baseline reserved GPUs, expected concurrency occupancy, recommended oversubscription factor, burst cushion in vGPU-hours, and an ops playbook for routing/fallback. I’ll also attach a short PDF (burst-budget-proposal.pdf) with two options (conservative vs optimized).

Can we lock the 45-min sizing workshop on Thu Sep 3 at 11:00 AM ET? Marissa — can you join to run latency/batching tradeoffs? Ben — please validate GPU SKU assumptions in the attached proposal.

Thanks — Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Pre-Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Attach: burst-budget-proposal.pdf

From: Ashley Park <ashley@vellumai.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@vellumai.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Traffic tiering & burst-budget intake for dedicated sizing — VellumAI

Nikhil — all good, and Sep 3 11:00 AM ET works for us. To answer your clarifications:

1) Bursts are single-region (us-east-1), typically from a small set of edge gateways.
2) Long-form jobs are mixed but trending asynchronous; however, we do route some long summaries in the interactive flow during demos.
3) KV cache hit-rate hovers ~38–45% today (we are working on improvements).
4) Correct on the quality split — 80/20 as you outlined.

Procurement, looping you in — we need a conservative SKU-level estimate for internal review. Ashley P. will coordinate an NDA/PO template if required.

Looking forward to the workshop.

Best,
Ashley
